I need produce only JSON object with declaration implementation supporting_objects. Should design CODESYS ST exact interface. Should decide helper DUT state enum perhaps supporting object. Should compile offline. Should have declaration FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task followed all VAR sections omit END_FUNCTION_BLOCK. Implementation body alone. supporting objects list DUT enum perhaps E_TaskState with declaration "TYPE E_TaskState :\n(\n IDLE,\n MOVING,\n COMPLETE,\n FAULT\n);\nEND_TYPE". CODESYS 3.5 ST. Make sure states globally perhaps enum names potential generic but okay. Or avoid supporting objects using INT internal state constants? Requirements "Use states IDLE, MOVING, COMPLETE and FAULT" best define DUT E_TaskState with values. Could use state : E_TaskState := E_TaskState.IDLE; enumerations in CODESYS support qualified. Could declare TYPE E_TaskState : (IDLE, MOVING, COMPLETE, FAULT); END_TYPE. State variable q : E_TaskState := E_TaskState.IDLE; Then implementation transitions priority.

Should think "first" atomic proposition perhaps not necessarily require first variable. Initial conditions pre-state IDLE outputs false. Outputs assigned every scan based on post-state. Should initial variable q initialized IDLE. At most one transition scan using IF ELSIF. Jam from any state sets FAULT even if already; reset no Jam sets IDLE. Latched fault if q FAULT no Reset and no Jam: remain. Stop abort non-fault to IDLE. Normal state case: IDLE Start and not AtExit => MOVING. MOVING AtExit => COMPLETE. COMPLETE hold. FAULT hold. Outputs after. Implementation:

IF Jam THEN
    eState := E_TaskState.FAULT;
ELSIF Reset THEN
    eState := E_TaskState.IDLE;
ELSIF eState = E_TaskState.FAULT THEN
    eState := E_TaskState.FAULT; (no transition)
ELSIF Stop THEN
    eState := E_TaskState.IDLE;
ELSE
    CASE eState OF
       E_TaskState.IDLE:
          IF Start AND NOT AtExit THEN eState := ... MOVING; END_IF;
       E_TaskState.MOVING:
          IF AtExit THEN ... COMPLETE; END_IF;
       E_TaskState.COMPLETE:
          eState := E_TaskState.COMPLETE;
       E_TaskState.FAULT:
          eState := E_TaskState.FAULT;
    END_CASE;
END_IF;

Belt := eState = ...; Complete etc.

Do I need Stop in IDLE with AtExit etc to IDLE yes. Stop in COMPLETE to IDLE. Jam priority over reset. Reset when Jam false any state to IDLE, including IDLE. Without Reset fault latched even Stop. Good.

Potential subtle: Jam TRUE while already FAULT remains. Jam FALSE Reset true clears. Start in IDLE AtExit true rejected. In test final step after reset with Start true AtExit true -> remains IDLE, outputs false. Then Start true Stop true AtExit false -> stop priority IDLE, good.

Declaration formatting:
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
    Start : BOOL;
...
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
...
END_VAR
VAR
    State : E_TaskState := E_TaskState.IDLE;
END_VAR

Perhaps include output init := FALSE? Not necessary, but initial conditions could explicit. "followed by all VAR sections" okay. Internal state name perhaps q. No VAR_IN_OUT. Use `FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task` no `END_FUNCTION_BLOCK`.

Supporting object each name kind declaration implementation. DUT implementation likely "" (empty string). User requires each with name, kind, declaration, implementation; functions return_type. For DUT implementation can be "". JSON valid newline escaped automatically in response. Only JSON. Could avoid helper by internal INT and local constants? But "Define referenced DUTs" implies okay to use enum. supporting object DUT. Should consider CODESYS syntax for enum and initialization qualified. CODESYS 3.5 enum can be `TYPE E_TaskState : (IDLE, MOVING, COMPLETE, FAULT); END_TYPE` and use `E_TaskState.IDLE`. Strict enum? Default enum allows qualified. Good.

Potential concern generic `COMPLETE` conflicts output `Complete` case-insensitive? Enumerator global `COMPLETE` and FB output `Complete` same identifier? In CODESYS, enum members may be globally available and inside FB scope output `Complete` could conflict? Qualified references avoids internal, but declaration of enum constant COMPLETE and variable Complete in FB perhaps no compile conflict because scoped. However in CODESYS enum values often must be globally unique vs variables? Local variable can share global enum component? Usually yes, local scope. But output `Complete` same name as enum literal `COMPLETE` could cause CASE? Qualified okay. Yet CODESYS enum declaration may generate global constant `COMPLETE`, and POU variable `Complete` is local, no conflict. Better name enum values `TASK_IDLE`, etc? Requirement states IDLE etc perhaps must use exact state names conceptually. Could use DUT with `IDLE`, etc. Fine.

Perhaps include `first` handling? Atomic propositions mention first but no explicit requirement except initial state. `State` initialization suffices. Outputs initial values default false. No first scan needed.

At most one state transition per scan: If Jam etc priority. CASE only one. Assigning same state not transition. Fine.

Perhaps no ELSE in CASE? All enum states covered. Good.

Could simplify latched fault ELSIF State = FAULT THEN `;` null statement not ideal. Use no-op assignment. Or structure:
IF Jam THEN ...
ELSIF Reset THEN ...
ELSIF State <> E_TaskState.FAULT THEN
  IF Stop THEN ...
  ELSE CASE ...
  END_IF;
END_IF;
This avoids no-op and latches. In CASE include FAULT branch optional? If State not fault, CASE only IDLE/MOVING/COMPLETE. Could still include all. Priority "latched fault" before Stop. Use:
IF Jam THEN ...
ELSIF Reset THEN ...
ELSIF State = E_TaskState.FAULT THEN
    State := E_TaskState.FAULT;
ELSIF Stop THEN ...
ELSE CASE ...
END_IF.

Outputs set after. Good.

Should have JSON no markdown. Ensure strings escaping newline. I can output pretty JSON with strings containing \n. supporting_objects DUT declaration. `implementation`: "".

Should I include `return_type` only functions, not DUT. Fine.

Could perhaps name DUT `E_TaskState` and kind `DUT`. Good.

I'll think if test harness expects no DUT perhaps okay. They will compile objects. CODESYS `TYPE E_TaskState :` syntax line. Use `END_TYPE` in declaration. All standard.

One subtlety: CODESYS enums when qualified with type name require `{attribute 'qualified_only'}`? Without it, qualified still allowed. yes.

One could use `VAR_STATE`? no.

Output initialization `Belt : BOOL := FALSE;` etc ensures initial conditions pre-scan but outputs assigned each scan. Fine. Exact interface names/types preserved; initial values don't change. Internal state `eState` initialization. No need `first`.

Stop aborts "a non-fault cycle to IDLE." My Stop from any nonfault including IDLE and COMPLETE. Good.

Normal transition in MOVING only AtExit. Start irrelevant. COMPLETE held until Reset or Stop, Jam also forces fault as required. "COMPLETE is held until Reset or Stop" plus jam overrides. Good.

Jam in IDLE sets fault. Reset with Jam false in IDLE remains IDLE. Start plus Reset reset wins.

Outputs based on post state. P4 valid idle start Belt same scan. P5 arrival Complete same scan. Good.

No timing.

I should respond.
